mint(address,string,bytes32,bytes).details: Operator (server wallet) typically calls this on behalf of the user         right after the user's first interaction. Owner can also mint directly.

params.hash_: Content hash binding the chain commitment to the blob.
params.initialSealedKey: Sealed symmetric key encrypted to `to`'s public key.
params.uri: 0G Storage rootHash of the encrypted metadata blob.

authorizeUsage(uint256,address,uint256,b.notice: Authorize an executor (e.g. a verified lawyer agent) to use this         agent's capabilities until `expiresAt`. permissionsHash binds to         an off-chain JSON describing what the executor may do.

authorizedUntil(uint256,address).notice: authorizeUsage: tokenId => executor => permission expiry timestamp (0 = revoked).

cloneAgent(address,uint256,string,bytes3.notice: Clone an agent's state into a new INFT for `to`. Use when a         user wants to spin off a sub-agent for a specific case while         keeping the original. Oracle signs over the new sealed payload.

contentHash(uint256).notice: Hash of the encrypted metadata blob (binds the chain commitment to the off-chain data).

isExecutorAuthorized(uint256,address).notice: Whether `executor` may currently act on `tokenId`'s behalf.

metadataURI(uint256).notice: 0G Storage rootHash holding the encrypted metadata blob.

mint(address,string,bytes32,bytes).notice: Mint a new Case Agent INFT to `to`.

sealedKey(uint256).notice: Sealed symmetric key: encrypted to the current owner's public key. Off-chain encrypts/decrypts.

sealedKeyOf(uint256).notice: ERC-7857 view: returns the bound sealed-key payload.

transferAgent(address,uint256,string,byt.notice: Transfer an agent to a new owner. Off-chain, the oracle has         re-encrypted the metadata blob with the recipient's public key         and produced a fresh sealedKey. The oracle's signature over         (tokenId, newURI, newContentHash, newSealedKey, to) is verified.

updateMetadata(uint256,string,bytes32).notice: Update the agent's encrypted memory pointer when the user has         new conversations or case events. Only the token owner (or an         operator they approved) may call this.
